region.finding: Fresh enlarged source and battle views show white lower muzzle and chin compressing toward the scarf during alternate idle/hit and folding in defeat. Independent upper-eye, muzzle and lower-lip probes retain neck/chest influence. Ears, frozen crest/back spikes, scarf, torso, four legs and complete tail separately inspected. Candidate requires independent face, complete geometry and repeated visual verification. Initial short chin-to-scarf transition passed face landmarks but produced seven whole-mesh warning poses and was rejected; soften the measured lower transition while retaining rigid lower lip coverage.

All 13 original body and skull clips visually inspected front/side. Lower lip and central-eye surround change shape on strike/recoil. Dense anatomical probe corroborates shape distortion. Candidate visual verification pending.

Fresh enlarged source and battle views show lower white muzzle compressing during alternate idle and hit, and pulling toward the scarf during defeat. Ears, eyes, headband tails, scarf, wrapped arms, torso, legs, feet and complete tail separately inspected. Preserve existing neck binding while completing the lower face.

All 24 enlarged released source/battle slices actually inspected. Eyes visibly shear and swell during idle, walk, gallop and combat; masked lower muzzle collapses toward the scarf on recoil and defeat. Whole affected face retains chest/spine/pelvis influence. Ears, headband tails, scarf, sword, arms, torso, legs, feet and tail separately inspected. Complete face repair must preserve the neck transition and pass all geometry checks. First candidate rejected: its low transition reached the left forearm and produced two stretched edges during attack. Raise the transition floor to preserve that forearm while keeping the full masked lower face rigid. A shorter transition caused eight warning poses and was also rejected. Test the smoother transition with precise weights to avoid quantization at tiny connected edges. Precise weights alone retained the measured forearm crease. Smooth its two measured connected edges while preserving the rigid face and lower-body bindings. Precise weights alone retained the measured forearm crease. Smooth its two measured connected edges while preserving the rigid face and lower-body bindings.

All 24 enlarged released source/battle slices actually inspected. Lower white muzzle compresses toward the scarf in alternate idle, hit and defeat; independent lower-lip patch retains neck influence. Eyes, tall ears, cheek fur, scarf, torso, four legs, feet and complete tail separately inspected. Incremental repair completes the exposed lower muzzle while preserving the reviewed neck elsewhere.
